value.name: prepare dinner for girls' night
value.description: The women are gathered at Sarah's beach house cooking, tossing salad, and pouring wine for a girls' night.
evidence: Pasta being cooked. Salad being tossed. Wine glasses are filled. It's Girl's Night at the beach.

value.name: marylin compares betrayal to godfather scene
value.description: Marylin explains that seeing Pat in court silenced her the way Frankie Pentangeli is silenced by seeing his brother in The Godfather.
evidence: MARYLIN It was like that scene in The Godfather. Frankie Pentangeli is called to testify against the Family. And he's in court, and he looks into the spectators gallery, and sees his Brother. They brought the brother from Sicily. And Frankie can't say a word. He can't testify. That's what it was like seeing Pat in there. I couldn't even have Ruth cross examine her.

value.name: ramona questions why pat betrayed marylin
value.description: Ramona asks why Pat would do it, prompting Marylin to speculate about money, a free trip to Los Angeles, or Massey's influence.
evidence: RAMONA Why do you think she did it?
MARYLIN (Shrugs) Maybe she wanted a free trip to LA. Maybe they offered her money. Massey is very seductive. Who knows.

value.name: ramona jokes about horse head threat
value.description: Ramona jokingly suggests that Pat may have been intimidated with a horse head in her bed.
evidence: RAMONA Maybe they put a horse head in her bed?

value.name: sarah condemns the betrayal
value.description: Sarah reacts with disgust, saying Marylin was left with nothing and that the situation makes her question the legal system.
evidence: SARAH That stinks. They left you with absolutely nothing. It makes you wonder about the entire legal system.

value.name: sarah compares case to rodney king
value.description: Sarah broadens her criticism by comparing the injustice of Marylin's situation to the Rodney King case.

value.name: marylin claims speech was bought
value.description: Marylin concludes that Pat's testimony was bought and argues that if she only wanted Rex's money, he should not have to pay her anything.
evidence: MARYLIN They bought her speech. If I was only in it for Rex's money, he shouldn't have to give me any.

value.name: ramona reframes marylin's motive
value.description: Ramona says Marylin's argument makes no sense and reframes it as punishing her for being goal oriented.
evidence: RAMONA That doesn't make sense. It's like punishing you for being goal oriented.
